title: Open subsets of a one-dimensional Noetherian local spectrum
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] whose Krull dimension is at most one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be its affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every open subset $W\subseteq S$, if the closed point $\mathfrak m$ belongs to $W$, then $W=S$; if $\mathfrak m\notin W$, then $W$ has a finite discrete underlying topological space and the induced open subscheme is affine. Here local means that the nonunits of $A$ form the proper ideal $\mathfrak m$; finite discrete means that there are finitely many points and every subset is open.

source.place: Tag 09N8 (lemma-affine), proof: reduction to the spectrum of a Noetherian local ring and the case analysis at the closed point; Algebra Tag 00FR and Schemes Tag 02O0

proof.text:
Every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ is contained in $\mathfrak m$: an element outside $\mathfrak m$ is a unit, and no proper ideal contains a unit. If $\mathfrak m\in W$, choose a basic Zariski open $D(f)$ with $\mathfrak m\in D(f)\subseteq W$. By the definition $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f
otin\mathfrak p\}$, we have $f
otin\mathfrak m$, so $f$ is a unit and $D(f)=S$. Thus $W=S$. In the remaining steps assume $\mathfrak m
otin W$.

If $\mathfrak p\ne\mathfrak m$ is prime, it is minimal: otherwise there is a prime $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p$, giving the length-two chain $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak m$, contrary to $\dim A\leq1$. For the same reason the only primes containing $\mathfrak p$ are $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak m$. This argument also includes dimension zero, when there is no prime other than $\mathfrak m$.

The ring $A$ is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] gives a finite set of minimal prime ideals of $A$. Every point of $W$ is a nonmaximal prime and hence, by step 2, belongs to that finite set. Therefore $W$ has finitely many points.

source.place: Tag 00FR (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), applied in the proof of Varieties Tag 09N8

proof.text: For $\mathfrak p\in W$, the Zariski closed set $V(\mathfrak p)=\{\mathfrak q:\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$ consists of $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak m$ by step 2. Since $\mathfrak m\notin W$, its intersection with $W$ is the singleton $\{\mathfrak p\}$, which is therefore closed in $W$. Given any point $\mathfrak p\in W$, its complement in $W$ is a finite union of the other closed singletons by step 3; hence $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is also open. Every subset is a union of these open singletons, so $W$ is discrete. For $W=\varnothing$ the same conclusion is vacuous.

The induced open subscheme with underlying space $W$ is a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Its space is finite and discrete by steps 3 and 4, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine] applies and makes it affine. That statement includes the empty scheme, so no nonemptiness hypothesis on $W$ is needed.
